flight-depth finding: VulkanRenderSurfaceContext::flightFrameSize = 1 makes getCurrentFrameIndex() always 0, so resolveFlightIndex always returns 0 and the render side's two-slot flight tables (RenderSubmissionPool, RenderViewOutputTable, viewFrameDataPerFlight, FrameUploadArena) only ever run slot 0 in production; measured as flight=0 on all 90 ticks of both smoke runs

flight-depth finding context: it stays safe because VulkanRenderSurfaceContext::begin calls waitAllGraphicsFences() before acquire, i.e. a wait-idle-per-frame policy consistent with flightFrameSize = 1; a real overlap would need flightFrameSize raised, the wait narrowed to frameFences[currentFrameIdx], and a check that slot 1 actually cycles -- recorded as a decision item, not changed

4d-3 closure: 4d-3b made the editor declare its panel rect every frame, which turned a latent uninitialized-geometry bug into a crash -- the editor exited 255 on the first frames when it ran right after a game run, with RenderGraph.cpp:1027 (zero texture extent) reached from SSAOStage::appendGraphPass

4d-3 closure root cause: Rect2D had no default member initializers and glm's default constructor is trivial, so EditorLayer's viewportRect / _viewportMouseRect / _viewportBounds[2] were uninitialized memory; uninitialized floats are commonly denormals (bits 0x00000096 / 0x00000001 were observed, and once (0, 1.17e27)), which pass an extent > 0 test, and Extent2D::fromVec2 then truncates them to 0

4d-3 closure: the declaration contract is now explicit -- a SceneViewDesc viewportRect must be finite and at least one whole pixel. Rect2D members are default-initialized, EditorLayer::describesPixels gates both notifyViewportWidgetRect and getViewportRect, and SceneRenderScheduler::submit rejects a non-finite or zero-rounding declaration at the single funnel every producer goes through

4d-3 closure evidence: the game-then-editor sequence crashed 3/3 before the fix and passes 8/8 after; runtime and editor viewport screenshots stay byte-identical (1c6668976be1cdd5d755d1f1365700f7 / 1bfb16e7ca543abb7b517325df508b90); ya-render-3d-test 174/174; the ya-testing filter 103/103

tickRender reads as its steps: prepareModules, prepareHostViewState, declareViews, extractScenes, prepareViews, buildGameRenderFrame, acquire, recordFrame, submitRecordedFrame, presentModuleExtras
the steps are private static members of GameRuntimeTickOrchestrator, so no new coordinator or packet layer was introduced and tickRender stays the only entry point

ownership: the SceneViewCollector and the UIFrameSnapshot are owned by tickRender and passed in, because the returned primary declaration and the camera packet point into them; a builder never returns a pointer to its own local

the order is unchanged from before the extraction, including the deviation the plan's text has: app.prepareModulesForRender runs first, ahead of prepareHostViewState and the view declaration, rather than after prepareViews as the plan lists it; reordering is a behaviour change that needs its own verification and is recorded as such

view-declaration policy lives in the producers since 4d-1/4d-2, so tickRender holds no 'should this view render' branch; the UI snapshot is produced by buildGameRenderFrame and never read from the live WidgetTree during recording

evidence: ya-render-3d-test 174/174, the ya-testing filter 110/110, and two game-then-editor smoke rounds (four runs) all exit 0 with zero log errors and four byte-identical screenshots -- a pure reordering of code, so nothing about the pixels or the flow changed

header cost: the step signatures take CameraFrameInput / ExtractedSceneRender / SceneViewCollector, so the orchestrator header forward-declares those types instead of including them; the MSVC-facing trap is -Wmismatched-tags, which rejects forward-declaring the class SceneRenderScheduler as a struct
